PC: Inquires about patient’s reason for seeking medical care
Gathers specific sexual history (5 P’s: partners, practices, protection from STIs, past history of STIs, and pregnancy intention) and provides appropriate resources and psychoeducation as necessary
Assesses for mood disturbances surrounding the menstrual cycle
Inquires about past, present, and intent for future use of HRT (e.g., testosterone)
Provides appropriate options for menstrual suppression in line with patient’s goals
SBP: Inquires about desire for name and pronouns to be included in patient medical record
ICS: Introduces self with name and pronouns
Inquires about patient’s chosen name and pronouns using affirming language
Uses inclusive language when building rapport with patient and gathering history
Uses warm and welcoming body language to promote relaxation and build trust
Uses gender neutral and/or anatomically correct language when referring to medical concerns and body parts
Provides patient education about the impact of HRT on the menstrual cycle, if applicable
Adequately describes when physical exams are necessary and collaboratively decides if an exam is necessary in today’s visit
Provides opportunity to discuss patient concerns or discomfort with physical exam (or any part of the visit) and addresses concerns with empathy
Learners will use shared decision making to create a personalized plan of care with the patient
